previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypertension, anxiety, and chronic back pain presented with worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and chills after being diagnosed with a suspected UTI in the ED. She developed hypotension requiring fluid resuscitation and norepinephrine, prompting ICU admission. Initial concerns for cardiac ischemia were ruled out with normal troponins and echocardiogram. Abdominal imaging showed chronic spine changes but no acute surgical cause. Chest imaging revealed mild pulmonary edema and crackles, leading to a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia, treated with levofloxacin. Her abdominal pain resolved, and labs showed transient anemia and thrombocytopenia that improved with treatment. Thyroid function tests suggested sick euthyroid syndrome. She stabilized, was weaned off pressors, and transitioned to oral antibiotics. Metoprolol was reduced due to hypotension. She was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor blood pressure, and follow up on thyroid function and mental health.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old with pmhx of CAD s/p CABG and PCI, 
HTN, HL, and anxiety who presents with 3 days of  burning with 
urination with increased urinary frequency found to have an 
E.Coli urinary tract infection. 

# E.Coli UTI. Patient presented with several days of dysuria for 
which she saw her PCP and was prescribed macrobid. She took 1 
dose and developed N/V.  On arrival to the ED, UA still mildy + 
and ultimately cultured out to E.Coli  She was started on 
ceftriaxone with symptomatic improvement. In the setting of her 
dramatic presentation decision was made to treat as a 
complicated UTI though transitioned to PO Ciprpfloxacin after 
reviewing the sensitivities. She remained hemodynamically stable 
throughout her stay and was discharged with plan to complete the 
remaining 3 days of treatment.

# Anemia/Thrombocytopenia. On review of OSH records cytopenias 
appears chronic with thrombocytopenia present since ___. 
Previous work-ups largely negative. In house, coags wnl, 
fibrinogen ~400, B12 712, retic: 2.5. In house counts remained 
stable. Will defer further work-up to the outpatient setting. 

# Lactic acidosis: Improved from 3.8 -> 3.1 after 2 L IVF in the 
ED. Etiology likely hypovolemia/sepsis physiology from UTI as 
well as N/V. 

# CAD: Resumed home dose metoprolol once stabilized. No 
complaints of chest pain in house. 
 
# Hypothyroidism: Continued home levothyroxine.

# GERD: Continued home omeprazole.

# Osteoporosis: Continued vit D

# Disposition. Patient deconditioned after illness and hospital 
stay. Note to be unsteady when walking with staff. Patient 
evaluated by ___ who deemed discharge to rehab optimal 
(anticipated length of stay less than 30days)
